answer: Each epoch the payout sits in a vault opened only by a cedar key: a receipt carved by an inspector who must wander through the agent's live work and sign one job it witnessed. Keys are carved only inside the epoch, never in advance, and one inspector visits at most three agents, so n clones need n visits from a scarce pool, each priced higher the more visits one trail requests. Inspectors finding the same job across clones void every key they carved and keep the bonds. So n clones pay n visits at rising prices yet open one vault share, while one honest agent pays once and keeps the catch.
